To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein L25 from E. coli has a stable, folded structure in solution, that the protein can be reversibly unfolded, and that the structure of the native protein can be characterized by proton NMR spectroscopy.
L25 can be reversibly folded and that its folded form is indistinguishable, by spectroscopic criteria, from that prepared by methods avoiding denaturing agents.

L25 can be reversibly unfolded by denaturing solvents; the folded form of L25 has an NMR spectrum which is indistinguishable, spectroscopically, from the form of the molecule prepared by methods which do not use denaturing solvents (i.e. the native form of the molecule); the folded form of ribosomal protein is a compact, globlular tertiary structure; primary assignments have been made for a numberof resonances in its proton NMR spectrum.

the characterisation of the folded form, and with the study of the unfolding process.
